title: Durable lane status artifact
description: The single on-disk record a supervisor reads to learn the state of a durable isolated lane without reading the conversation. Written at or before the acknowledgement and updated in place; the identity fields are immutable once written. The record is flat: one level of keys, with structure only where a field is genuinely a set. The write lease is a separate record in its own file and is not referenced from here at all — the lease names this artifact by filesystem identity, so the binding runs one way and the two records can fail independently.

schema.description: Schema name and version of this artifact, so a file written long ago is read under the rules it was written under.

lane_id.description: The lane's durable identifier, adopted from the spawn result. Immutable. A worker may append to or targeted-edit this artifact but may never overwrite an identity field; a mismatch produces an identifier-propagation blocker instead of a delivery.

runtime_run_id.description: Which run inside the runtime is executing the lane. Immutable, and adopted from the spawn result rather than from a planning slug, a proposed branch name, or any pre-spawn placeholder.

child_session_key.description: The isolated child session the lane runs in. Immutable, and adopted from the spawn result.

origin_message_id.description: The inbound message that caused this lane. Immutable. Every other record in the chain carries it too, so the chain can be reassembled from any one of its parts.

delivery_target.description: The route the result is owed to. Immutable.

state.description: Lifecycle state. The last eight are terminal and collapse to six outcomes, because two of them accept a spelling variant; of those six only complete is success-terminal, and cancelled or superseded lanes own no worker-visible final at all. The artifact must hold a terminal state before the visible final is sent.

health.description: The health vocabulary, additive to state and never inferred from it. Prefer the narrowest truthful class; the list is descriptive, not a severity ladder. When there is no fresh evidence at all, the honest output is not a class but a request for verification from outside the runtime.

acceptance_level.description: How strong the evidence behind the result is. It rises only when evidence a reader could open exists under the lane's artifact root; a level above not-yet-verified with nothing recorded to support it is a defect.

scope.description: The declared objective this lane owns, written before execution so a later step can be tested against it rather than against memory.

single_worker_reason.description: Required when fan-out stayed at one worker. Writing it down is what keeps a lane that ran alone on purpose distinguishable from a fan-out that silently failed to launch.

write_boundaries.description: The declared write boundary, stated in both directions. An empty allowed list is a defect: the boundary is what makes an out-of-scope edit detectable.

phases.description: The named progress ladder with per-phase state. A checkpoint is owed when one of these transitions, not when a timer expires.

checkpoint_due_within_minutes.description: When the next operator-visible update falls due. Staleness has to be measurable, not felt.

checkpoint_delivery_strategy.description: How that update will be sent — for example at phase boundaries rather than on a fixed interval.

owed_final_type.description: What kind of terminal result this lane owes. The obligation is created at acknowledgement time and clears only on a visibly delivered final or an explicit cancellation.

blockers.description: Open blockers, typed rather than written as prose. A state of complete while a blocker row is open is a defect.

source_route_exercised.description: The route that was actually exercised, or null when none was. This keeps the route was tried and failed distinct from the route was never attempted.

next.description: The next atomic action, and who owns it.

diagram_artifact.description: Where the diagram this lane produced was written, when it produced one. Null otherwise.

delivery_state.description: How far the owed delivery has got.

delivery_message_id.description: The provider message id for the final. Completion is proven by the provider, not by the sender, so this stays null until one confirms.
